title: Emulating the Forced Response of Climate Models with Generative Machine Learning
abstract: arXiv:2605.16929v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Global climate models are essential tools to simulate past and potential future pathways of climate change, as well as associated climate impacts. Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) describe a range of future scenarios of global economic and demographic development. These SSPs are intrinsically linked to changes in climate forcings -- the external drivers, such as greenhouse gas and aerosol emissions, which change Earth's energy balance over time. These forcings act as boundary conditions in Earth System Models (ESM), providing insight into the potential climatic impacts of each SSP. Running an ESM, however, is extremely computationally expensive, conflicting with the need for large ensemble runs to provide robust estimates in the presence of internal variability and scenario uncertainty. translated_title: 使用生成式机器学习模拟气候模型的强迫响应
translated_abstract: 全球气候模型是模拟过去和未来潜在气候变化路径以及相关气候影响的重要工具。共享社会经济路径（SSPs）描述了全球经济和人口发展的一系列未来情景。这些SSP与气候强迫的变化有着内在联系——气候强迫是指外部驱动因素，如温室气体和气溶胶排放，它们会随时间改变地球的能量平衡。这些强迫在地球系统模型（ESM）中作为边界条件，为每个SSP的潜在气候影响提供洞察。然而，运行ESM的计算成本极其高昂，这与需要大集合运行以在内部变率和情景不确定性存在的情况下提供稳健估计的需求相冲突。机器学习模拟器为快速、低成本地生成气候情景提供了一条有前景的途径，但直到最近还缺乏不确定性量化。
tldr: 该论文提出利用生成式机器学习来模拟气候模型对气候强迫的响应，从而以极低的计算成本快速生成气候情景，并实现不确定性量化。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes using generative machine learning to emulate the forced response of climate models, enabling fast and low-cost climate scenario generation with uncertainty quantification.
